title: Tenant lease & fallback: hybrid throughput escrow and progressive shedder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with Dedicated capacity require firm per-tenant throughput guarantees while allowing safe burst behavior and graceful degradation when the fleet is constrained. Current admission controllers are per-request token buckets and static queue depth limits; they either over-provision or produce hard rejects under transient spikes.
proposal_summary: Introduce a hybrid "token escrow" (lease-based) admission system per-tenant that: 1) reserves steady-state throughput windows (leases) backed by fleet allocation; 2) accumulates unused lease credit into a short-term burst escrow that can be consumed; 3) implements a progressive shedder that demotes, deprioritizes, or routes to lower-cost fallbacks instead of hard-dropping when headroom is exhausted. The controller emits autoscaler hints and backpressure signals to the Dedicated autoscaler to trigger soft scaling earlier than current thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-tenant lease mechanism enforces configured minimum throughput (e.g., 100 RPS) under nominal load with +/-5% jitter
2) Escrow converts unused lease capacity into burst tokens with time-to-live configurable (default 30s)
3) Progressive shedder stages: priority demotion -> synthetic throttled-200 with causal header -> hard reject; all stages are observable in Console
4) Autoscaler receives hints and reacts in test harness within configured window (default 60s) without oscillation in 2/3 load patterns
5) End-to-end integration test shows improved tail latency and lower rejected-request ratio vs baseline under mixed tenant spikes
implementation_notes: Control plane: lease allocation API to be added to capacity manager (new /v1/leases endpoints). Leases are short-lived (TTL'd) and renew via lightweight heartbeat.
Serving layer: admission proxy maintains per-tenant in-memory escrow state; supports atomic consume/return operations with optimistic concurrency.
Fallbacks: route demoted requests to compatible cheaper model variant (quantized) or to a cached response path when available.
Autoscaler integration: emit hint events (Hop/Hint) with expected headroom delta; implement dampening to avoid scale thrash.
Telemetry: add token consumption, escrow balance, demotion counts, and hint events to per-tenant metrics (Prometheus and Console traces).
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle, escrow accounting, and edge cases (clock skew, renew race)
Load harness: simulate 200 tenants with mixed steady and spiky traffic and compare rejected-ratio and 95/99p latencies to baseline
Chaos test: kill X% of fleet nodes and verify progressive shedding behavior and autoscaler hints prevent mass hard-rejects
Canary: rollout to a single Dedicated pool with two non-critical customers for 72h before broad rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flagged behind tenancy opt-in; unit + integration tests merged
Phase 1: Canary on non-production Dedicated pool for 72 hours
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 20% of Dedicated capacity with monitoring dashboard and auto-rollback triggers
Phase 3: Full rollout and retire old hard-queue admission controller after 2 weeks of stable metrics
metrics: Rejected request ratio by tenant (target < 0.1% under normal load)
Escrow utilization and average burst consumption window
95/99th latency for guaranteed vs. opportunistic requests
Autoscaler hint-to-scale latency and scale outcome (successful/rolled-back)
risks: Lease starvation if control plane incorrectly over-allocates — mitigated by conservative defaults and canary monitoring
Autoscaler thrash due to noisy hinting — mitigated by dampening and min-hint-interval
Complexity in debugging demoted responses — mitigated by causal headers and tracing propagation
Edge-case of long-running streaming responses consuming burst tokens — add separate accounting path for streams
